answer: An agent must first root a cedar proof by sealing sequential memory offsets under a time-locked seed, then the verifier walks a yarrow-sampled chain of cache-line probes that only local DRAM can complete inside the inlet of a 20-nanosecond budget. One honest identity pays the cost once; a farm of 500 aliases must buy 500 separate RAM banks and still lose every probe that crosses a network boundary, so the attacker's bill scales linearly while rewards do not.
